subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: Should startup and runtime recovery reclaim current-gateway-PID session locks when HELD_LOCKS has no matching entry, including legacy no-starttime or too-old same-process locks, or should OpenClaw continue preserving those locks until stronger liveness proof exists?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves some live current-PID OpenClaw locks to avoid false-positive deletion, while field reports show that same conservatism leaves real sessions wedged and an open PR proposes a broader cleanup policy.

options.title: Approve a narrow reclaim policy
options.body: Repair or replace the open cleanup PR so current-PID locks are reclaimed only when HELD_LOCKS is empty for that session and the lock is unchanged, with active-lock and legacy tests.

options.title: Keep conservative preservation
options.body: Leave current behavior in place, close or reject the open cleanup PR, and document that operators should use `openclaw doctor --fix` or manual cleanup for ambiguous live locks.

options.title: Require heartbeat/lifecycle proof first
options.body: Defer broader reclamation until lock files carry holder progress or lifecycle state that can distinguish a stuck live holder from a legitimate long write.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow reclaim policy
recommendation.body: Repair or replace the open cleanup PR so current-PID locks are reclaimed only when HELD_LOCKS is empty for that session and the lock is unchanged, with active-lock and legacy tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across the session-write-lock policy and adjacent recovery behavior.
